stack.engine: smoltcp 0.11.0 (std, medium-ip, proto-ipv4, proto-ipv6, socket-tcp, socket-udp)
stack.device: bounded Medium::Ip RX/TX queues (256 packets each), MTU from configuration
stack.registry: one Stack per configuration fingerprint; Weak entries; idle-with-no-sockets stacks stop their poller and are dropped
stack.tcp: smoltcp tcp::Socket behind AsyncRead/AsyncWrite; poll_shutdown sends FIN; remote FIN is EOF; RST is ConnectionReset; connect timeout is TimedOut; limit is OutOfMemory naming the maximum
stack.udp: unconnected smoltcp udp::Socket, many destinations per association, oversized datagram is InvalidInput naming the MTU

wireguard.peer_selection: longest matching allowed-ips prefix; equal lengths: later peer wins; missing prefix is a named no-route failure
wireguard.carrier: tokio tasks; bind_udp anti-loop; persistent-keepalive timer; one rekey after an authentication failure
verified: IPv4 ICMP echo through the locked wireguard-go device
IPv4 UDP echo through the locked device and the L3 stack
IPv4 TCP echo through the locked device and the L3 stack
IPv4/IPv6 stack behaviour and MTU bounds against the independent in-tree peer
not_verified: IPv6 through the Go wireguard-go peer (the fixture only answers IPv4)

openvpn.carrier: one dedicated OS thread owning the blocking control/data link; connect in the async task resolves the server through outbound::resolve_all; the thread waits for the stack and then pumps send_data/recv_data(10ms)
verified: control channel, TLS and key-method 2 against OpenVPN 2.7.9
send_data accepted and the session remains usable
connect_stack builds from the pushed ifconfig and opens a UDP socket
not_verified: delivery of TCP or UDP payload through a real OpenVPN tunnel: the controlled server runs --dev null and discards IP packets

consumers.tcp: outbound::dial_inner Protocol::Wireguard / Protocol::OpenVpn return a real stream; no DIRECT fallback
consumers.udp_engine: engine.rs serve_udp_associate_inner has WireGuard (guard option.udp) and OpenVPN send/receive arms over one L3 UDP socket
consumers.udp_tunnel: tunnel/udp.rs Transport::L3 shared by WireGuard and OpenVPN; the association resolves domain targets through the existing IP-only helper

anti_loop.wireguard: outbound::bind_udp in connect_endpoint and the stack entry point
anti_loop.openvpn: udp_socket_std_blocking / tcp_stream_std_blocking for the control link

tests.default_suite: pass (217 lib tests plus every default integration suite, --test-threads=1)
tests.device_vpn_suite: pass, including l3_stack 8/8; the desktop-tun command (which enables device-vpn) also passes

concerns: OpenVPN payload delivery through a real tunnel is not end-to-end verified; the controlled server runs --dev null. Only control/data-channel wiring, PUSH_REPLY and stack construction are proven.
IPv6 through the WireGuard fixture is not verified (the locked Go peer only answers IPv4); IPv6 is covered by the independent in-memory L3 peer.

The option matrix was not regenerated (needs a release kernel plus the pinned Mihomo baseline); its existing ip-stack rows remain accurate because mips/gVisor are still rejected, only the rejection text changed.
target/t35 is a private build cache created for this attempt and is not part of the change; the shared target directory was not used.

WireGuard handshakes every configured peer eagerly when the stack is created; one unreachable peer therefore fails stack creation even when the target would use another peer (the pinned device connects lazily per peer).
